absent: Locking, sleeping, and concurrency rules for ethtool netlink, epoll, eventfd, fadvise, and ext4 ioctls.
State machines and sequencing for cable tests, firmware flash, power sourcing negotiation, and timestamp configuration.
Numeric values of O_CLOEXEC and O_NONBLOCK and ioctl encoding widths, and epoll busy poll semantics.
Meanings of ext4 tune fields, feature words, mount option bytes, checkpoint effects, and shutdown levels.
Netlink header layout, attribute types and lengths, error reporting, and privilege requirements.
Handler behavior for fadvise values 4 and 5 and for unlisted ethtool attribute values.

findings.text: Most ethtool attribute and message enumerations reserve value zero for an unspecified or none entry, assign consecutive small integers to members, then close with a private count sentinel and a public maximum one less than that count, so the maximum is the highest valid identifier and the count is the table size.

A minority of ethtool enumerations start at one instead of zero and still close with count and maximum, including the forward error correction histogram pad member, the flow classifier ether member, the power notification header member, and the mean square error capability snapshot and top level members; the clause 33 power limit maximum uses a doubly underscored private name.

First routed ethtool range covers transmit low power enable and timer, timestamp transmit packet lost error and unconfirmed one step counters, hardware stamp provider index and qualifier, timestamp info combining header timestamping transmit kinds receive filters clock index statistics provider source and phy index, cable pair result code and source with fault distance in centimetres and nest grouping, cable and reflectometry headers with notification status and configuration over first last step and pair, and tunnel UDP port type entries in tables with size and type set under tunnel info. Examples are the timestamp phy index, fault centimetre, and tunnel table entry members.

Second routed range covers correction histograms by low high value and per lane values with corrected uncorrected and bit counts plus modes automatic active and statistics, module EEPROM access by offset length page bank address and data, statistics groups with identity counters and bucketed histograms plus header and source, virtual clock count and index, module power policy and state, single pair and clause 33 power sourcing with administrative state control delivered status class actual and available power extended state and priority, scaling hash indirection key and transform, collision avoidance config and status, firmware flash file password status and progress, PHY topology names, timestamp config provider and filters, power events, and error capabilities snapshots and channels.

The flow classifier enumerates about two dozen link and network and transport and tunnel selectors starting at one for ether, covering IPv4 and IPv6, TCP UDP SCTP AH ESP and combined AH ESP, and GTP user and control plane with tunnel endpoint header uplink and downlink variants, closed by count and maximum. Out of order examples are the downlink user GTP IPv6, ether, and SCTP IPv4 members.

User to kernel ethtool commands provide get set and action operations for string sets, link info modes and state, debug, wake on LAN, features, private flags, rings, channels, coalescing, pause, energy efficient ethernet, timestamp info, cable test and reflectometry actions, tunnel info, correction, module EEPROM, statistics, virtual clocks, module, power sourcing, receive scaling creation deletion and set, collision avoidance config and status, MAC merge, firmware flash, PHY, timestamp config, and error snapshot. Out of order examples are the error snapshot get, string set get, and scaling create action.

Kernel to user ethtool messages provide get replies and change notifications for the same subsystems, with none valued zero and reply and notification variants distinguished in the name, plus a monitor multicast group whose name is the word monitor. Out of order examples are the scaling delete notification, string set reply, and power notification.

Eventfd creation flags comprise a semaphore mode occupying bit zero with value one, a close on exec flag that aliases the generic O_CLOEXEC value, and a nonblock flag that aliases the generic O_NONBLOCK value.

Epoll control operations are add one, delete two, and modify three. Low event bits are input 0x1, priority 0x2, output 0x4, error 0x8, hangup 0x10, invalid 0x20, normal and band read 0x40 and 0x80, normal and band write 0x100 and 0x200, message 0x400, and peer shutdown 0x2000. High bits are bit 27 wake for user rings, bit 28 exclusive, bit 29 wakeup, bit 30 one shot, and bit 31 edge triggered. Close on exec aliases O_CLOEXEC.

Epoll event carries a poll mask followed by a 64 bit user datum and is annotated with a packing macro. Epoll parameters carries a 32 bit busy poll microsecond value, a 16 bit busy poll budget, an 8 bit prefer busy poll flag, and an 8 bit pad so the size stays a multiple of 64 bits. The ioctl type is 0x8A with number 0x01 to set parameters and 0x02 to get parameters, both transferring the parameters structure.

The epoll packing macro has two build dependent spellings, one expanding to a packed attribute and one expanding to nothing, so the event layout is identical on the wire but the compiler padding guarantee differs by configuration.

Ext4 ioctls use type f for version, reservation, group extend and add, migrate, delayed allocation flush, extent move, resize, boot swap, extent precache, extent status cache clear and query, state, checkpoint, UUID get and set sharing number 44 with opposite directions, and tune parameter get and set, plus type X number 125 for shutdown. A 32 bit compat family mirrors version reservation and group operations with int width and a compat group input. Out of order examples are shutdown, version get, extent move, and compat group add.

Filesystem UUID carries a 32 bit length, 32 bit flags, and a trailing flexible byte array for the UUID. Extent move carries a reserved 32 bit word, a donor descriptor, two 64 bit logical start block offsets for origin and donor, a 64 bit requested length, and a 64 bit moved length. New group input carries a 32 bit group number, three 64 bit absolute block numbers for block bitmap inode bitmap and inode table start, a 32 bit block count, a 16 bit reserved block count, and a 16 bit unused field.

Tune parameters starts with a 32 bit select mask and check interval, error behavior mount and max mount counts and RAID stride as 16 bit fields, last check time reserved blocks and block count as 64 bit, default mount options reserved user and group and stripe width as 32 bit, encoding and encoding flags as 16 bit, hash algorithm plus pads, three current feature words, three set masks, three clear masks, a 64 byte mount option area, and 68 bytes of trailing pad.

Ext4 state bits are precached 0x1, new 0x2, new entry 0x4, and delayed allocation close 0x8. Checkpoint bits are discard 0x1, zero out 0x2, dry run 0x4, with a valid mask combining all three. Going down modes are default zero, log flush one, and no log flush two. Tune select bits run from errors behavior 0x1 through encoding flags 0x20000. The fiemap hole extent flag is 0x08000000.

File access hints are normal zero meaning no special treatment, random one, sequential two, will need three, dont need six, and no reuse seven. Values four and five have no assignment in the routed fragments.

Native and compat ext4 ioctls differ in operand width so callers must use the matching width and group input shape. The UUID structure has a flexible tail so callers must size it by the length field. The extent move reserved word is documented as zero and the new group unused field has no defined value. Checkpoint callers must restrict flags to the valid mask. UUID get and set share one number with opposite transfer direction.
